The volume of total crude oil and petroleum product imports fell in August to 287.4 million barrels from 319.7 million in July. The total value fell to $5.46 billion in August from $5.89 billion. These data are available only on a Census basis.

The price of imported crude oil rose to an average $18.65 a barrel in August from $18.24 per barrel in July. The value of August crude oil imports fell to $4.30 billion from $4.67 billion, the department said.
The U.S. trade deficit with China in August was a record and surpassed that of Japan as America's largest monthly bilateral gap for the second time this year.

A steep drop in U.S. exports of transportation equipment to China and a sharp rise in American imports of Chinese-made toys and Christmas decorations were behind the surge in the bilateral deficit in August, the department said.

The balance-of-payments basis for recording U.S. trade via receipts from and payments to other countries includes adjustments for military shipments, nonmonetary gold, and inland freight trade with Canada and Mexico.
Census basis data uses information collected by the U.S. Customs Service on goods shipped across U.S. borders.
